audit.why: 48.91% over 276 games is close to even, but Fiora genuinely owns levels 1-3 against a jungler kit with an 18s-at-rank-1 Arctic Assault. Difficulty 4/10 for the lane phase is defensible; the loss comes after items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart gave Levels 4-5, First item and 2+ items all to Fiora, while the packet chart reads Skill/Skill/Sejuani and the page's own whys[3], whys[5] and whys[6] say exactly that ('It evens out', 'stays a skill matchup', 'She out-scales').
audit.why: The chart contradicted the prose sitting next to it on the same page.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 -> Skill, First item -> Skill, 2+ items -> Sejuani, with phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten so the reasons match the sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions that Fury of the North's Frost Armor grants slow immunity, and Riposte's stun condition is stated loosely.
audit.why: Riot text: 'After being out of combat, Sejuani gains Frost Armor which grants Armor and Magic Resist and immunity to slows.' While that holds, Bladework's first-hit slow and any Lunge on-hit slow simply do not apply — she walks out of your chase at full speed. Separately, three of her casts are immobilizes Riposte converts into a stun: Arctic Assault's knock-up, Permafrost's stun, and the Glacial Prison bola. Her passive also lets her shatter a stunned target for heavy magic damage, so eating Permafrost is not just lost tempo.
audit.corrected: Riposte her Arctic Assault knock-up, Permafrost stun or Glacial Prison — each is an immobilize, so the parry stuns. Expect no slow to land while Frost Armor is up.

audit.why: The mirror flagged a systemic 'Permafrost passive' fusion on Sejuani pages; this page keeps Permafrost (E, stun at max Frost stacks) and the armour separate, so no fix is needed here.
